question: A 47-year-old man, with a history of a right parotid pleomorphic adenoma, treated with surgery (extrafacial parotidectomy) 6 months ago, who came to our clinic because he presented pain during the mastication with sweating and reddening of the skin of the preauricular region. What treatment would be the one of choice?

options.opa: Total parotidectomy enlarged when suspicion of tumor recurrence.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "History of right parotid pleomorphic adenoma" -> "Possible recurrence of tumor" -> "Symptoms of pain during mastication" -> "Sweating and reddening of skin in preauricular region" -> "Suggestive of Frey's syndrome" -> "Botulinum toxin can reduce sweating" -> "Injection of intradermal botulinum toxin is effective" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Post-surgical symptoms" -> "Pain during mastication" -> "Sweating and reddening of skin" -> "Indicates possible nerve damage or Frey's syndrome" -> "Total parotidectomy is more invasive" -> "Botulinum toxin is less invasive and targets symptoms" -> "Injection of intradermal botulinum toxin is preferred" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Surgical history of parotid tumor" -> "Symptoms of pain and sweating" -> "Possible Frey's syndrome" -> "Botulinum toxin can alleviate symptoms" -> "Less invasive than total parotidectomy" -> "Injection of intradermal botulinum toxin is the best choice" -> 88%

CHAIN: "Post-operative complications" -> "Pain during mastication" -> "Sweating and reddening of skin" -> "Suggests nerve involvement" -> "Total parotidectomy is not necessary unless recurrence is confirmed" -> "Botulinum toxin is a symptomatic treatment" -> "Injection of intradermal botulinum toxin is indicated" -> 87%
analysis: The symptoms described, including pain during mastication, sweating, and reddening of the skin in the preauricular region, suggest a possible case of Frey's syndrome (gustatory sweating), which can occur after parotid surgery. The most effective treatment for Frey's syndrome is the injection of intradermal botulinum toxin, which can help alleviate the symptoms by blocking the nerve signals that cause sweating. Total parotidectomy is not indicated unless there is a suspicion of tumor recurrence, and broad-spectrum antibiotics would not address the underlying issue. Pregabalin is used for neuropathic pain but is not the first-line treatment for this condition.
